Dispositions

Your temperament, not your talent. Each one changes a part of your life:

Emotional Stability: how fast stress builds and clears, and how much Composure you start with.
Conscientiousness: how well you sleep, and how much Discipline you start with.
Ambition: how fast stress builds, from work and from money alike.
Risk Tolerance: above 65, your card’s autopay starts out paying only the minimum, so you carry a balance.
Extraversion: whether performing in front of people, an audience or your class, raises your stress or eases it.
Openness: whether rehearsing new work, a festival’s new play or a Cabaret piece, lifts your morale or lowers it.
Agreeableness: whether a day of rehearsal lifts your morale or lowers it.

Apart from your starting Composure and Discipline, none of these makes you a better or worse actor. Composure is one of the abilities your performances are judged on.

Traits

Pick up to four. Traits come in opposing pairs, and you can’t have both of a pair. Between them, they change:

how fast stress builds and clears;
how well you sleep, and how much a night restores;
how soon you need a shower;
how far your morale swings;
how hard an illness hits;
how sharp you are in the morning or the evening;
which part of preparing a scene goes furthest;
how you warm to classmates, and how much a slight from one hurts;
and, for Frugal, Spender and Generous, what your food costs and how much a meal lifts you.

A trait’s description and cost describe the whole person, but the game uses only the effects above. Once you’re playing, open a trait on your Player Profile to see exactly what it changes.

0 / 4
TEMPERAMENT
Even Tempered
Very little gets through. Bad news lands on you the same way good news does.
People read the calm as not caring, and drift away from it.
Quick Tempered
It comes up fast and it’s gone just as fast, which isn’t much comfort to whoever was standing there.
Stress arrives quicker and relationships wear.
Highly Strung
You feel everything at full volume. It’s exhausting, and it’s where the work comes from.
Stress builds fast and sleep is the first thing to go.
Unshakeable
Whatever happens, you’re the one still thinking clearly twenty minutes later.
You’re slow to notice something is genuinely wrong, including with you.
Sentimental
Birthdays, first drafts, the people who were there at the start. You keep all of it.
Endings go badly, and you hold on well past the point of any use.
Detached
You can put a thing down and walk away from it, including people.
Everything you have drifts unless you tend it: a classmate comes closer more slowly.
HABITS
Early Riser
Up before anybody wants you, and the best hours of your day are over by ten.
An evening call finds you flat: rehearsals and performances get less of you.
Night Owl
The good hours start after midnight, and none of them are before noon.
Every morning class is a fight with yourself, and you sleep badly.
Orderly
Everything has a place and you notice immediately when it isn’t in it.
Disorder costs you more than it costs other people.
Chaotic
The mess is genuinely invisible to you, and it never weighs on you.
It shows on you sooner.
Homebody
Your own bed is where you recover, and it puts more back than most.
A full room does less for you: friends in a cast lift you less.
Restless
Stillness is beyond you, and a room full of people is where you come alive.
You don’t rest properly, and a cast without a friend in it weighs on you.
BODY
Disciplined
The training, the sleeping, the eating: all of it belongs to a person who means to still be working at sixty.
The hours it takes are hours you aren’t spending on anybody.
Indulgent
Late food, late nights, and the firm belief you’ll deal with it later.
You’ll deal with it later, and it will cost more then.
Resilient
Illness, injury, a bad year: all of it clears faster in you than in the people around you.
None. This one is simply luck.
Burns Out
You can go very hard for a long time and then you can’t go at all.
The crash is real, and it always arrives at the worst moment.
Light Sleeper
A door, a car, a thought. Anything wakes you and then that’s the night gone.
You’re never quite rested, and it accumulates.
Sleeps Anywhere
Floors, chairs, the twenty minutes between two things. You take it where you find it.
None. Like Resilient, it’s simply luck.
MONEY
Frugal
You know what everything costs, and the day’s food costs you less.
The cheap version every time: a meal does less for your morale.
Spender
Money is for turning into things, and a good meal lifts you more than most.
It goes out faster than it comes in, and it always has.
Generous
You pick up the check, you lend it and you don’t chase it.
People remember it fondly and you’re poorer for it.
Keeps Accounts
What you’re owed and by whom, down to the coffee, stays remembered.
So does everybody else, about you: a slight cuts deeper both ways.
PEOPLE
Loyal
The people who were there at the start are still there, and always will be.
You stay long after you should have gone, and it wears on you.
Independent
You don’t need the room, the company or the reassurance. You’re fine.
Nobody is quite sure they matter to you, and eventually they stop trying.
Needs People
You’re better with somebody in the room. You always have been.
Alone, you come apart quietly and quickly.
Guarded
It takes a long time to get anywhere with you, and almost nobody has.
The few who did are load-bearing, and there aren’t many of them.
An Open Book
You say the thing. People know where they are with you within about a minute.
Keeping a thing to yourself has never once happened.
Peacemaker
You can feel a room going wrong before it does and you get in front of it.
You absorb the trouble and then carry it around all day.
Holds Grudges
Exactly what was said, by whom, and in what year: it’s all still there.
It costs you people, slowly, over a very long time.
Forgiving
It goes, genuinely, and the next conversation starts from nothing.
You let the same thing happen twice, and carry it both times.
MIND
Curious
The thing nobody asked you to read gets read, and you go deeper into how to play a part.
It isn’t useful now, and now is when the work is due.
Single Minded
One thing at a time, all the way to the bottom of it: lines drilled until they’re yours.
Everything else does exist, and it piles up while you’re down there.
Scattered
Six things at once, all of them moving: you get around a scene fast.
Most of them, anyway: something is always the one you dropped.
Self Critical
You’re the harshest critic you’ll ever have, and a revision is better for it.
It isn’t free. It comes out of you.
Self Assured
What you can do is settled, and nobody has ever needed to confirm it for you.
You’re the last to hear that something isn’t working.

Your Body

Your height and weight on the first morning. In feet, inches and pounds, the units of the United States, where you live.

Height (Feet)
Inches
Weight (Pounds)

Leave them blank and SLATE picks them at random, around the averages where you were born. Once you’re playing, your weight changes with what you eat and how active you are. A heavier body is more likely to develop diabetes, high blood pressure and arthritis over the years, at published rates, and a weight far from the middle either way makes a long life less likely.

Where It Begins

You’re a first-year in the MFA in Acting at the David Geffen School of Drama at Yale University, one of 16 actors admitted this year: among the strongest of them, but not ahead of everyone.

You arrive in New Haven on August 24, 2026, the first day of the fall term. Tuition is covered, as it is for every student.
